status: Major allocation hot spot and resident categories identified; no release acceptance or universal leak-free conclusion.

malloc.boundary_inuse_caveat: Includes tcache/fastbins; not precise live objects. Virtual free chunk size is not resident memory.

quickjs.caveat: Matched exact binary allocator table and runtime initialization offsets. QuickJS logical malloc accounting differs from arena reserved/resident accounting; do not subtract the two to assign ownership.

other_resident_details.caveat: Pages containing metadata are not an exclusive byte ownership census; mixed mappings and non-atomic reads remain. About 1 MiB of other pages is still not assigned to a specific owner.

limitations: Allocation deltas are global counters inside the UNION of source-probe/signature intervals; overlapping scopes are counted once.
This establishes time coverage, not exclusive allocation ownership or retained-byte attribution. Concurrent non-scan allocations can contribute.
Same-SHA independent prior allocation call stacks provide direct ownership evidence for scanner allocations.
Low-frequency four boundary probes; no malloc-level instrumentation, no GC intervention.

conclusions: Current business uses the older source_probe/source_signature path; four refresh threads execute about 40 probes and 4 signatures per second combined.

Global allocation increments are 99.85% temporally covered by the union of source scope intervals; this is not exclusive per-allocation ownership. Same-SHA isolated allocation stacks directly demonstrate scanner allocations.
Boehm whole free blocks plus glibc free top are large resident categories. Natural GC reuses/frees object memory without returning all resident pages.
Four identified QuickJS runtimes account for about 8.02 MiB logical allocations and were unchanged in the short repeat; does not establish long-term absence of JS leaks.

No new runtime/vlang/vjsx source changes, package deployment, restart, target function calls or forced GC. Four low-frequency scope probes and 15-second CPU sampling were temporary; first metadata-only parser attempts failed closed.
limitations: One 15-second-later natural-GC census failed consistency checks and is excluded.
CPU perf sample had only 12 events and unreliable optimized user-frame unwinding; do not use for quantitative caller attribution.
About 1 MiB of other resident pages and ownership of remaining native allocations are still unresolved.
These are production passive diagnostics, not a workload controlled comparison or a 24-hour acceptance run.
next_actions: Exercise the existing low-allocation scanner candidate independently with representative four-engine source layouts before business deployment. Preserve same-size/same-mtime content detection and scope isolation.
Compare resident high-water, repeated traffic/cooldown and latency; allocation reduction alone is insufficient.
Keep aggressive per-collection unmapping disabled; leave bodytest and existing monitoring intact.
